body:
Triage: healing a half-annotated card — `domain:engine` was already right (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`) and stays; adding the pm-state and type it was missing. Type **Task**: quote style in operator-facing prose, no behaviour and no declaration involved.

**State `pm:on-hold` with an opportunistic trigger — and this is a direct answer to the question the card asks and declines to judge**: *"whether this is worth its own PR versus being picked up alongside a future touch of this file."* ⇒ **The second, and the hold is the mechanism that makes it happen rather than a way of forgetting it.** A quote-character swap does not earn its own dispatch, its own branch, its own CI run and its own queue slot; discarding it loses a real (if small) inconsistency against a 174-vs-37 convention. The rider path costs nothing and lands it correctly.

Restart-when: any dispatch whose declared file surface includes `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` — this card is then a pre-declared rider on that card, to be folded in and closed with it.

Restart-touch: packages/objectql/src/registry.ts

⭐ Note this wake condition is genuinely **reachable**, which is why a hold is legitimate here and was refused on two other cards today (#12760, and the repair of objectui#5453). The `Restart-touch:` line feeds the H17 on-hold trigger-file index that dispatch reads at claim time and intersects against the card's file surface — so the wake happens by a mechanism someone actually runs, not by someone remembering. ⛔ A hold whose trigger nobody reads is the exit-less park the state machine forbids; this one has a reader.

**When it does wake**: the shape is likely a bare quote-character swap plus a literal-spelling pin, mirroring what #12609 did on the sibling guard (no existing pin was found on this message either) — ⛔ but that is the card's own "not established", so the rider confirms it rather than assuming it.

⭐ **Crediting the scope discipline that produced this card**, because it is the behaviour that makes riders cheap: #12609's dispatch said *"Touch the one message"* twice, and the dev **did not fold this in** even though it is nine lines away and the same defect class. It is a genuinely different message (`ships from package` / "will shadow", the late-registration order) with its own test coverage in `registry-collision-order.test.ts`. Folding it in would have been the *"package-wide sweep buries the fix"* failure that dispatch explicitly warned against. ⇒ Filing it instead is exactly right, and the hold is what keeps that discipline from costing anything.

Also credited: the measurement re-derived the convention rather than citing it (174 single vs 37 double over non-test `.ts` in `packages/objectql/src`), and **explained the 4-count difference from the earlier report as a different regex rather than a different tree** — ⛔ not waved away as noise. That is the reverse-check standard this lane asks for.
